bull_bear.body: Priority on debt reduction via asset monetization (10 assets sold in FY26; 6 pending). Expected cash inflow: INR 750 Cr+ by June '26, INR 400 Cr by Dec '26. Deferred consideration of ~INR 550 Cr expected over 24-36 months. Working capital debt target: INR 500-600 Cr by Mar '27.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Execution delays due to land acquisition/clearances (ROW). Working capital stretch (debtor days elevated to 5-7 months in Power, 3-3.5 months in Roads). Regulatory uncertainty on NHAI debarment clauses regarding site casualties. Geopolitical risks in international markets.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously optimistic; acknowledges FY26 as a 'transition year' with execution challenges but emphasizes strategic consolidation, balance sheet strengthening, and clear visibility on FY27 recovery through monetization and new order flow.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Significant order book value (INR 2,000 Cr+) resides in SPVs (Saudi/IGR) and does not reflect in standalone ABL order book but will consolidate. ECL provisions are transient; reversals expected as milestone payments clear, artificially suppressing current margins. Deferred monetization proceeds (~INR 550 Cr) tied to NHAI toll extensions create a hidden future cash flow stream.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Asset monetisation is the stated capital-efficiency lever: "ACL's HAM portfolio, including the Kharar-Ludhiana, Ranastalam-Anandpuram, Ankleshwar-Manubar Expressway, and Khairatunda-Barwa Adda Road projects, was successfully monetised and moved off the books in September 2025", along with ABL's Kandi-Ramsanpalle HAM, "further strengthening the company's balance sheet and enhancing capital efficiency".
- The 5 HAM projects sold in September 2025 are quantified as Sale Consideration 1,146 (ACL 4 HAM 965 + ABL 1 HAM 181), Cost of Investment 599 (530 + 69) and Profit 547 (435 + 112) Rs. Crs.
- "The BOT portfolio comprising of Ashoka Highways (Bhandara), Ashoka Highways (Durg), Ashoka Belgaum Dharwad Tollway, Ashoka Sambalpur Baragarh Tollway, and Ashoka Dhankuni Kharagpur Tollway was monetized by the company in November 2025".
- Consolidated debt has been taken down sharply across the five quarters shown: 6,826 (Jun'25), 4,910 (Sep'25), 2,718 (Dec'25), 2,778 (Mar'26), 2,773 (Jun'26) Rs. Crs., split at Jun'26 into Project Debt Incl ACL Debt 1,600 and Standalone Debt 1,173.
- Standalone debt of 1,173 is composed of Working Capital Loan 1,110, Equipment Loan 63 and NCDs (ABL) shown as "-"; cash & bank balance at Jun'26 is 261 standalone and 943 consolidated (Rs. Crs.).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Road EPC (50% of Q4 rev), Road HAM (10%), Power T&D (18%), Railway (8%), Others (14%). International wins include Saudi Arabia (INR 900 Cr share), Angola (INR 690 Cr), Liberia (INR 430 Cr). Domestic bridge win in Bihar (INR 242 Cr share).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply chain constraints and input cost inflation impacting EPC margins across the sector. | UltraTech Cement | beneficiary | Med | Ashoka cites rising cement prices as a key cost pressure; volume recovery in FY27 guidance supports demand. |
| Delayed payments and working capital stretch in power T&D segment. | Power Grid Corp | loser | Low | While not directly named as debtor, Ashoka's comment on 5-7 month billing cycles in power suggests systemic payment delays affecting upstream equipment suppliers too. |
| Need for private capital participation in road infrastructure (BOT model push). | IRB Infrastructure | beneficiary | Med | Govt target of INR 75,000 Cr BOT projects in FY27 benefits established players with monetization track records like Ashoka and peers. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Legacy slide claims "50+ YEARS of experience in construction industry", "16,000+ LANE Kms. of highway constructed", "30,000 Villages illuminated through Power T&D projects" and "10,000+ members in Ashoka Family".
- Order Book of "Rs. 15,251 Crs. Order Book as on 30th June 2026*", with the footnote "* Excluding orders received post 30th June 2026 of Rs. 451 crores"; the quarterly series reads Jun-25 15,886, Sep-25 14,888, Dec-25 15,927, Mar-26 15,312, Jun-26 15,251.
- Credit standing shown as "ACUITE RATINGS AA (stable)/Reaffirmed Long Term" and "A1+/Reaffirmed Short Term", alongside "0.49x Debt Equity Ratio (Standalone)".
- Execution credentials are showcased via signature projects: "India's First 8 Lane Extra Dosed Cable Stayed Bridge Built in 33 Months" across the Narmada river, "One of India's Longest 6 Lane Flyovers in Kerala (12.752 Kms)" (Aroor-Thuravoor above NH 66), and the Mopa Airport Link Road, Goa ("Project Length : 6.58 km with elevated portion of 4.4 km", piers as high as 40 meters).
- Bundelkhand Expressway (UPEIDA) was "completed ahead of schedule" with three construction records: non-stop laying of 12,765 tonnes of DBM in 64 hours, 19,756 tonnes of bituminous concrete in 96 hours, and 13 concrete deck slabs in 46 days.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Divestment] Subsidiary Ashoka Purestudy Technologies Private Limited (APTPL) allotted 29,879 equity shares of Rs.10/- each on a preferential basis to a new investor on June 12, 2026; ABL's holding diluted from 59% to 39.33% and APTPL "has ceased to be a subsidiary and is now an Associate Company" with effect from June 12, 2026.
- [Regulatory settlement] Following the NHAI Show Cause Notice dated November 26, 2025, the Company and NHAI signed a Settlement Agreement; "NHAI has agreed to close the proceedings with no further action against the Company, including withdrawal of the suspension and confirmation of no debarment, against payment of Rs.1.04 crore by the Company, deposited with NHAI on July 9, 2026."
- [Monetisation timeline slip] Sale of the remaining six SPVs of Ashoka Concessions Limited to Epic Concesiones 2 Private Limited / Infrastructure Yield Plus II & IIA (managed by EAAA India Alternatives Limited) has been extended again - to September 15, 2026 for TS-1, TS-2 and TS-3 "where major construction works are complete" and to September 30, 2026 for the BS SPV, subject to conditions precedent and regulatory/lender approvals.
- [Governance] Promoter-led management with Mr. Ashok Katariya (Chairman, founded the Company in 1976), Mr. Satish Parakh (MD, associated since 1982), Mr. Sanjay Londhe and Mr. Ashish A. Kataria (Whole Time Directors) and Mr. Paresh Mehta (CFO, CA with 33+ years, 26+ years with the group); the Board carries four Independent Directors.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: FY26 margins pressured by project prolongation, fixed cost absorption on lower turnover, and INR 28 Cr ECL provision in Q4. Input cost inflation (cement, steel, bitumen) cited as headwind. FY27 guidance assumes 9.5-10.5% margins factoring in potential ECL reversals as payments clear.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: ~20% for FY27. EBITDA Margin: 9.5%-10.5% (double digit). Order Inflow Target: INR 8,000-10,000 Cr. Capex: ~INR 100 Cr for FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Total: INR 15,312 Cr. Breakup: Roads & Railway INR 10,123 Cr (HAM INR 1,619 Cr, EPC Roads INR 7,084 Cr, Railway INR 1,420 Cr); Power T&D INR 4,627 Cr; Buildings INR 562 Cr. Excludes INR 900 Cr (Saudi Hotel) and INR 1,100 Cr (IGR Mumbai) executed at SPV level.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Monetization of remaining 6 HAM SPVs (4 by June '26, 2 by Dec '26) releasing ~INR 1,150 Cr cash + deferred consideration. International pipeline expanding in Middle East and Africa. Bid pipeline >INR 1 Lakh Cr (INR 40k Cr NH + INR 30-40k Cr States/others).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Ashoka Buildcon navigated a transitional FY26 with revenue degrowth (-17% YoY) due to execution delays and conservative accounting (ECL provisions), but successfully monetized 10 assets to strengthen the balance sheet and secured high-value international orders (Saudi Arabia, Angola) that position FY27 for a 20% revenue rebound and margin expansion to double digits.

meta.thesis: Ashoka Buildcon navigated a transitional FY26 with revenue degrowth (-17% YoY) due to execution delays and conservative accounting (ECL provisions), but successfully monetized 10 assets to strengthen the balance sheet and secured high-value international orders (Saudi Arabia, Angola) that position FY27 for a 20% revenue rebound and margin expansion to double digits.
